text: NARVIK, Sept. 18 — The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 240 megawatts, according to people familiar with the matter. The figure was confirmed in a technical filing circulated this week by operator Halcyon Marine Grid, which said the facility’s four turbine strings were designed to deliver steady output through winter peak demand. People familiar with the matter said the project, located on the outer fjord near Kelsa Point, is now in final commissioning after more than six years of work. Halcyon plans to begin phased commercial generation in November, with full capacity expected by early 2027, the people said.
